prompt: 200mm telephoto compression down a data hall rack row, one high-density compute cabinet off-centre lower-left with its session slots packed to the rail; its model-writer blade glows amber under a hard top light while adjacent tool blades stay cool blue, braided fibre queue cables bunch at the front like stalled traffic. rationale: The story is about scale and capacity—sessions per box on a live serving cluster—so a compressed telephoto view of a data hall rack row makes the bottleneck legible as physical infrastructure rather than a literal screenshot. The treatment is allowed and appropriate after recent work.
cue: sessions per box against a cache budget
subject: one high-density compute cabinet whose session slots are packed to the rail, its model-writer blade glowing hot while adjacent tool blades remain cool
core_thesis: An agent runtime's room is consumed by whole sessions rather than single calls, so the cap that matters is sessions per box against a cache budget, and exceeding it taxes the model's writing time while tools remain comparatively idle.
core_conflict: Write-path persistence versus tool-idle slack under a cache budget; over-admitting sessions throttles model decode while tool execution stays underutilised.
composition: Extreme asymmetry; overloaded cabinet lower-left third, empty breathing room right, telephoto flattening the row

review.depicts: A close-up of a server cabinet in the left foreground packed with rows of vertical drive and compute modules, with a band of drive bays lit orange-yellow and lower bays lit blue, and a coiled bundle of thick cables looped in front of it, while a data-center aisle with more cabinets recedes out of focus to the right.
review.reason: It shows the physical 'box' whose slots are packed and one hot zone against cooler neighbors, which is the article's mechanism of capping sessions per cabinet and the strain landing on the model-writing unit, though it stops short of distinguishing tool blades from a writer blade and reads partly as generic data-center imagery.
